stories.title: LHC summons Punjab home secretary, Kot Lakhpat jail superintendent in plea seeking release of Imran’s sisters
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Thursday summoned the Punjab home secretary and the superintendent of Kot Lakhpat jail in connection with a petition seeking the release of former prime minister Imran Khan’s three sisters.
It stated that Imran’s sisters remained at Lahore’s Kot Lakhpat jail despite the lapse of the 30-day period of their detention.
In Wednesday’s petition, Shahrez contended that the detention period had expired, but the three sisters remained in custody.

stories.title: Karachi judicial magistrate rejects bail plea of anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan
summary: KARACHI: A local court on Thursday rejected TV anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan’s bail plea in a cybercrime case pertaining to the alleged dissemination of anti-state content.
Earlier this week, Hassan was sent to prison on judicial remand after the NCCIA sought an extension of his physical remand by another eight days.
The court also issued notices to the NCCIA on a bail application filed by Hassan’s defence counsel, Barrister Mian Ali Ashfaq, and fixed the matter for hearing on Oct 21.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz chairs apex committee meeting in Peshawar; to review security situation in KP
summary: The Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on October 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.
Governor Kundi, along with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, chaired a meeting of the apex committee a day after governor’s rule was imposed.

Federal ministers have also alleged that the PTI-led government in KP had a “nexus” with terrorist groups, stating that the province’s security situation necessitated the imposition of emergency there.

stories.title: LHC issues notices to foreign secretary in contempt cases over detention of PTI-linked Pakistanis in UAE
summary: On September 14, the LHC had directed the foreign secretary to process and decide within 15 days representations concerning the detention of two citizens — Syed Salman Raza Zaidi and Muhammad Junaid Jahangir.

The counsel for the petitioners submitted that despite representations having been filed regarding the detention of both citizens before the foreign secretary, the representations had not been processed.

Both petitioners had asked the court to direct that legal and consular assistance be provided to Zaidi and Jahangir, that their judicial records be obtained and that diplomatic-level steps be taken toward their return to Pakistan.

stories.title: Suspects in West Bank settler attacks put under house arrest
summary: All but one of the suspects arrested over recent settler attacks on an American photojournalist and a visiting French mayor in the West Bank have been released from detention and placed under house arrest, their lawyers said.
The incident comes 10 days after settlers beat an AFP photographer covering the West Bank olive harvest, Jaafar Ashtiyeh, leaving him also requiring hospital treatment.
Violence has flared in recent months in the West Bank, with near-daily attacks, thefts or vandalism by Israeli settlers against Palestinians.

stories.title: India capital steps up air pollution controls ahead of winter
summary: India began annual measures on Thursday to tackle toxic air pollution in New Delhi, a megacity of 30 million people regularly ranked among the world’s most polluted capitals.

In previous years, such measures have failed to curb pollution, which peaks from November to January, when levels of cancer-causing PM 2.5 microparticles often hit more than 300 micrograms per cubic metre, 20 times the World Health Organisation’s recommended daily maximum.
Last year, pollution levels peaked at 846 micrograms per cubic metre, 56 times the WHO limit.

stories.title: The Trump rally: a slice of 'Americana' politics, coming to an end
summary: Supporters wait for US President Donald Trump to speak during a campaign rally at T.
Supporters attend a rally of US President Donald Trump in support of Republican US Senate candidate Darline Graham ahead of the midterm elections, at T.
Header image: US President Donald Trump gives a thumbs up as he walks past the audience at a rally in support of Republican US Senate candidate Darline Graham ahead of the midterm elections, at T.

stories.title: Noor Zaman stuns defending champion Gawad to reach Silicon Valley Open quarters
summary: Pakistan’s Noor Zaman stunned defending champion and world No. 4 Karim Abdel Gawad of Egypt 3-1 on Wednesday to reach the quarter-finals of the PSA Gold Silicon Valley Open at the Redwood City in California.
Noor, ranked among the world’s top 35 players, had earlier booked his place in the last 16 with a 3-1 victory over American wildcard Bransten Ming.
The PSA World Tour Gold event offers equal prize money for men and women as squash prepares for its Olympic debut at Los Angeles 2028.

stories.title: What you need to know about the 2026 US midterm elections
summary: Democrats are also fighting to win the Senate, where Republicans hold a 53-47 majority.
If Democrats manage to win the House, the next speaker second in line for the presidency after the vice president is likely to be Democratic Representative Hakeem Jeffries of New York.
Also high on Democrats’ list of House seats they hope to take from Republicans are two in Pennsylvania and one in New Jersey.

stories.title: Lahore Gymkhana’s low rent attributed to ‘decades of oversight failures’
summary: Appearing before the committee alongside members of the club’s management, Mr Siddique expressed surprise at the nominal rate given the vast acreage involved and the club’s vastly improved financial footing.

Committee members noted that this admission from the club’s own top leadership underscored the urgency of determining why successive state authorities allowed such a massive concession to persist without meaningful scrutiny.
They stressed that the onus rested squarely on public institutions mandated to protect state land, enforce lease terms, and ensure transparent usage.

stories.title: Websites down: What is PHP and how has it raised AI hacking fears?
summary: Artificial intelligence has found critical security flaws in a major programming language called PHP, with many websites taken offline Thursday as organisations worldwide scramble to fend off would-be hackers.
It is “a backbone of the web”, according to security firm Wiz Research, which says it used AI to find vulnerabilities hidden in PHP for more than a decade.

Header image: Unplugged LAN network cables at a computer server, as cyber agencies warn that websites may be taken offline while PHP prepares a critical fix, in Berlin, Germany, on October 21, 2026. —Reuters

stories.title: Rawalpindi lawyers boycott courts over FIR against advocate for ‘assaulting’ judge
summary: RAWALPINDI: The contents of a sealed first information report (FIR) registered against an advocate for allegedly hitting a civil judge with a glass, injuring his head and fingers, in his chamber at the judicial complex on Tuesday have emerged.
Protesting against the registration of the FIR against the advocate, the Rawalpindi Bar Association boycotted court proceedings and staged a protest at the judicial complex on Wednesday.
The complainant added that when he and other court staff members tried to rescue the judge, Muhammad Farooq Aslam Khan and his companions assaulted him, causing him to fall to the ground.

stories.title: NAB seeks lowering of graft threshold to Rs50 million
summary: The NAB chairman claimed to have recovered state land worth trillions of rupees from encroachers, including 235,622 kanals of Pakistan Railways (PR).

Recovery claims According to NAB’s Director General (Operation) Amjad Aulakh, the bureau had retrieved state land worth Rs9.18 trillion in the third quarter of the current year, bringing the total recovery of the bureau to Rs11.524 trillion since 2023.

The NAB chairman said after making a record recovery of PR land, the bureau’s next target was to unveil corruption in the power sector, Evacuee Trust Property Board, state-owned enterprises, mines and minerals.

stories.title: Man sentenced to death for raping stepdaughter by Islamabad sessions court
summary: ISLAMABAD: An additional district and sessions court has sentenced a man to death for sexually assaulting his stepdaughter over a period of about a year, resulting in the birth of a child, and ordered him to pay Rs3 million in compensation to the victim and the child.
The court also ordered him to pay Rs1 million in damages to the victim and Rs2 million in compensation to the child born as a result of the assault.

According to the verdict, failure to pay the amount awarded to the victim would entail a further six months of imprisonment, while failure to pay the compensation awarded to the child would result in another six months behind bars.

stories.title: Man flees after allegedly raping minor girl in Vehari
summary: BAHAWALPUR: A man allegedly raped a minor girl in Suleman Town in the limits of Burewala Saddar police precincts in Vehari district on Wednesday.
The girl, on returning home, informed her father about the incident, who reported the matter to Burewala Saddar police.
MURDER CASE ‘SOLVED’: Gaggo Mandi police claimed to have solved the blind murder case of a young girl, who was allegedly killed for “honour” by her father and his accomplices at Chak 229/WB.

stories.title: Peshawar High Court seeks govt response to petitions about school collapse
summary: PHCBA President Aminur Rehman Yousafzai and lawyer Fawad Jan appeared on behalf of the petitioners and told the court that the building of a private school, Al-Khair Education System, near Ring Road collapsed on Oct 15, killing 31 students and a teacher.

Citing information available in public reports, the petitioners claimed that the school building was not constructed or maintained according to approved plans, structural standards, fire-safety requirements and emergency exit regulations.

The counsel argued that the tragedy pointed to broader weaknesses in the regulatory framework governing school registration and inspection, approval and monitoring of building plans, land-use compliance and administrative oversight.

stories.title: One dies in ice factory gas leak in Rahim Yar Khan
summary: RAHIM YAR KHAN: One person died while three others were affected after inhaling ammonia gas leaking in an ice factory near Sajjad Town on Shahi Road, some 35km from here, on Wednesday.
According to Rescue 1122 sources, on being informed about gas leak near Khanpur, Rescue 1122 teams rushed to the scene and plugged the leak.
One of the four persons, who were affected by the gas, and shifted to the Khanpur Tehsil Headquarters Hospital, later died.

stories.title: 11 hospitalised after drinking milk ‘supplied under CM scheme’
summary: Education CEO says cartons of milk used by family carry Jan 12, 2027, expiry date The police report stated that the family had consumed milk distributed at the school, following which their condition deteriorated.

Meanwhile, Abdul Sattar, one of the affected family members, alleged in a video clip circulating on social media that the school administration had distributed the milk to students under the CM Punjab Milk Programme.

However, a report issued by the Fort Abbas district education officer on Oct 21 stated that 132 of the 155 students enrolled at the school had consumed milk distributed under the programme, but no complaints of illness had been received.

stories.title: Labourer killed in boiler explosion in Karachi
summary: KARACHI: A labourer was killed and another injured in a boiler explosion inside a private chemical company in Port Qasim on Wednesday, police and rescue services officials said.
They added that workers were busy with some welding work when the boiler exploded.
The officials said that Waheed, 45, was admitted for treatment.

stories.title: ATC acquits three Muttahida activists in May 12 violence cases for want of evidence
summary: KARACHI: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Wednesday acquitted three men associated with the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) in three identical cases related to the May 12, 2007 carnage for lack of evidence.

Defence counsel says accused Mirza Naseeb and Raees Mama will remain behind bars as other cases against them are pending trial At the hearing, Umair appeared on bail, while the other two accused, Mirza and Raees, were produced from jail.
Speaking to Dawn, defence counsel Mushtaque Ahmed said Mirza and Raees would remain in jail as cases against them were still pending in court.

stories.title: Five men charged with PPP UC chairman’s murder in Karachi's Orangi Town acquitted
summary: KARACHI: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Wednesday acquitted five accused allegedly involved in killing of a union committee (UC) chairman belonging to the Pakistan Peoples Party in Orangi Town.
The case was registered under terrorism and murder charges by the Pakistan Bazaar police.

According to the prosecution, the accused Shahbaz and Shehzad were arrested in an illegal weapon possession case and during interrogation, they had allegedly confessed to their involvement in the murder of the UC chairman.

stories.title: Cabinet body discusses findings of Mir Raza judicial commission
summary: KARACHI: A cabinet subcommittee formed to oversee the implementation of the report of a judicial commission regarding the death of Mir Raza Ali met here to discuss the findings and a mechanism for their implementation.
The judicial commission’s report, which was made public by the provincial government on Tuesday, recommended, among other things, formation of a joint investigation team to probe the case.

According to a press release, the sub-committee reviewed matters relating to the implementation of the report and decided to submit its recommendations to the Sindh chief minister as soon as possible.

stories.title: IMF forecasts 1.3% contraction in Pakistan, 6.6% growth in 2027
summary: The International Monetary Fund said the region's output was expected to contract by 1.3% as a result of the war's ​impact on energy production, shipping, tourism, trade and confidence.

The war's impact had been substantial, but uneven, with oil-exporting ​economies directly affected by disruptions to energy production and shipping hit harder, and oil ​importers proving to be more resilient, the IMF said in its regional outlook released Thursday in Dubai.

Oil ⁠importers had proven more resilient, with domestic demand supported by remittances and tourism flows, favorable financial conditions, and prompt policy responses ​that safeguard consumers from higher commodity prices, the IMF said.

stories.title: Maldives president, CDF Munir stress importance of strengthening defence cooperation
summary: Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and visiting Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu underscored the importance of strengthening bilateral defence cooperation on Wednesday, state-run Radio Pakistan reported.

20 MoUs signed Pakistan and the Maldives signed a series of MoUs aimed at deepening bilateral relations in multiple sectors, including defence, IT, cybersecurity, health, education, social protection, agriculture and tourism, among others.
Muizzu, speaking to Dar, “expressed Maldives’ desire to deepen its close relations with Pakistan and explore new avenues of mutually beneficial cooperation”, the FO said.

stories.title: PSX plunges over 1,400 points as selling pressure mounts
summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) came under selling pressure in Thursday’s session, with the KSE-100 Index falling 1,421.85 points, or 0.86 per cent, to 164,509.13 by midday.
Read: PSX gains 779 points amid partial recovery Index-heavy names such as OGDC, PPL, MARI, HUBCO, PSO, HBL and UBL traded lower.
By early afternoon, the Index was trading near its session low, with the broader market reflecting cautious sentiment.

stories.title: Balochistan assembly panel okays whistleblower protection bill
summary: QUETTA: A provincial assembly committee on Wednesday advanced the Balochistan Whistleblower Protection Bill 2026 for final approval, bringing the proposed law designed to shield citizens who expose government corruption and administrative misconduct one step closer to enactment.

The Standing Committee on Services and General Administration Department (S&GAD) conducted a detailed and clause-by-clause review of the bill before recommending its submission to the house for approval.

The legislation aims to provide legal protection to individuals who disclose information in the public interest regarding corruption, abuse of authority and administrative irregularities in government affairs.

stories.title: Islamabad High Court seeks evidence against NAB officials’ appointments
summary: Chaudhry, observed that the petitioner had “completely ruined the entire case” after he argued that Mr Nasir had improperly described himself as a former judge despite having served only as an additional judge of the Lahore High Court (LHC).
The petitioner contended that Mr Shah had previously served as NAB prosecutor general, a position that did not qualify him as a federal government officer in Grade 21 or its equivalent.

Regarding Mr Nasir, the petitioner argued that he did not meet the criteria under Section 8(a) of the NAO, which requires a NAB prosecutor general to be qualified for appointment as a Supreme Court judge.

stories.title: China's natural disaster losses hit $30b in first nine months of 2026
summary: China recorded 199.36 billion yuan ($29.9 billion) in direct losses from natural disasters in the first ​nine months of 2026, mainly driven by severe typhoons, flooding ‌and landslides, its Ministry of Emergency Management said on Thursday.
"Several sudden extreme disasters in southern regions led to a significant increase in deaths and missing persons compared to the five-year average," the ministry said.

Read: Xi calls for improving disaster prevention as floods, landslides batter China Overall, 1,162 ​people have died or have been classified as missing from ​China's natural disasters in the first nine months of the year, up from 742 ‌a ⁠year earlier.

stories.title: Doctors confirm Pope Leo XIV requires no further treatment after lung surgery
summary: Pope Leo XIV’s doctors confirmed a day earlier that he would not require further treatment following surgery to remove a nodule from his lung, according to Vatican News.

Doctors said in a written statement that the removed tumour was a lung adenocarcinoma and that the disease was localised. “A subsequent oncological assessment has confirmed that no further treatment is necessary,” they reportedly said.
Read: Pope addresses crowd after cancer surgery The Vatican said the 90-minute operation was successful and that the lower lobe of his right lung was removed using video-assisted surgery.

stories.title: Sri Lanka elect to bowl against England in ODI tri-series
summary: Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis won the toss and elected to bowl first against England in their ODI tri-series match at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Thursday.
Fernando made a 39-ball 49 when Sri Lanka stunned England at Headingley during the 2019 World Cup.

Hopefully, we get some runs on the board and put them under pressure.” Sri Lanka: Avishka Fernando, Kamindu Mendis, Kusal Mendis (capt/wk), Pavan Rathnayake, Sahan Arachchige, Janith Liyanage, Dasun Shanaka, Dunith Wellalage, Eshan Malinga, Asitha Fernando, Dilshan Madushanka.

stories.title: Kharmang celebrates colour, taste and aroma of Suspolo apples
summary: GILGIT: The vibrant colours, sweet taste and captivating aroma of indigenous Suspolo apples took centre stage at the 7th National Suspolo Festival 2026, held in Pari Valley of Kharmang district, celebrating the region’s unique agricultural heritage and hardworking farmers.

Organised by the district administration with the support of the Gilgit-Baltistan Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries Department, the festival brought together Governor Mehdi Shah, Forests Minister Raja Nasir Ali Khan, locals and domestic and foreign tourists.

Speaking to Dawn, Deputy Commissioner Kharmang Nisar Ahmed Khan said the annual festival, held during the harvest season for the past seven years, aims to promote the indigenous apple, showcase local culture and help farmers find better markets for their produce.

stories.title: Mahnoor snares Sindh's first gold
summary: Sindh's Mahnoor Fatima on Thursday was crowned champion of the women's 5,000 metres race walk event of the 54th National Athletics Championship which exploded into action at the NED University of Engineering and Technology on Thursday.

WAPDA’s Ammara Manawwar claimed silver, while Punjab’s Sawera secured bronze. “It is the first day of the National Athletics Championship, and I won a gold medal for Sindh in the 5000m race walk,” Mahnoor said. “I would like to thank organisers for holding this event.
In the men’s 20km race walk, Waqas secured gold for WAPDA, with Navy’s Muhammad Younis Khan taking silver.

stories.title: North Korea threatens South with 'most horrible' consequences, announces border countermeasures
summary: North Korea warned South Korea of the "most horrible and distressing situation" if Seoul continues what Pyongyang described as interference, announcing new countermeasures along their heavily militarised border.
She said anti-South Korean loudspeakers would be ready for deployment along the border within days, signalling a further escalation in tensions between the two neighbours.

Read: South Korea orders stern response to any North Korean provocations amid border tensions Kim warned that continued interference by Seoul would trigger severe consequences, although the specific actions that prompted her latest warning were not immediately clear.

stories.title: ‘Letting roots of Pak-India conflict fester invites more danger’
summary: Gen Hayat warned that repeated crises between the nuclear-armed neighbours could become increasingly dangerous if unresolved disputes, diminishing restraint and the absence of sustained political dialogue continued to undermine regional security.

He said South Asia lacked an inclusive regional security framework, effective crisis-management mechanisms and sustained political dialogue. “The region lives between deterrence that prevents the worst and disputes that repeatedly regenerate danger,” he said.

Gen Hayat warned unverified allegations could trigger conflict before the facts were established, with a future confrontation potentially arising from an accident rather than a deliberate state decision.

stories.title: Saudis intercept more drones as conflict with Houthis spirals
summary: The Houthis denied having targeted the kingdom, with military spokesman Yahya Saree saying their forces had not carried out any “deep” operations in Saudi territory.

Egypt to support Saudis Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Wednesday that Cairo’s proposed military support for Riyadh was to “defend Saudi territory, and does not include an attack on Yemen,” state-linked media reported.
Sisi had asked lawmakers to approve military support for Saudi Arabia if requested by the kingdom, which has come under near-daily attacks from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.

stories.title: PTI leadership ‘turns on itself’ after protest debacle
summary: The bad blood became public on Wednesday as two senior party leaders — Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and former KP chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur — traded accusations of betraying the party cause.

This prompted the secretary general to take a dig at “the narrative” regarding a possible announcement by a group of party MPAs, nominating a new provincial president without permission from their jailed leader Imran Khan, or the party’s political committee.

Ali Amin Gandapur The secretary general accused the group of cutting off contact with Sohail Afridi and his team in the final days of the protest march, paving the way for state coercion, emergency and governor’s rule in the province.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine exchange strikes as US envoy leaves after talks
summary: The Russian strikes wounded 15 people and damaged subway infrastructure on the Southern Bridge over the Dnipro River in the Ukrainian capital while also restricting traffic there, ​Kyiv authorities said.
A Russian strike killed a woman and injured another four people ⁠in the Kharkiv region in Ukraine's northeast, Regional Governor Oleh Syniehubov said on Telegram.

In Russia, two people were wounded ​near Moscow after 630 drones were sent towards the capital during the night, Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said on Telegram. ‌Most ⁠of the drones were downed at long range, he added.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz arrives in Peshawar for apex committee meeting, security briefing
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif arrived in Peshawar on Thursday to attend an apex committee meeting on the law and order situation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), with a major development package for the province also expected to be announced during his visit, sources said.

The visit marked Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s first trip to Peshawar since the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on October 11, which resulted in the suspension of the provincial government led by Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI).
The first provincial Apex Committee meeting following the imposition of governor’s rule was held at Governor House on October 12, co-chaired by Governor Kundi and Interior Minister Naqvi.
